_doc: THE registry of legal disposition_owner values for PDS ledger rows. A non-empty disposition_owner is NOT evidence of ownership: before this file the field had no schema, no validator and no writer anywhere in api/lib or internal/, so a census could only assert 'non-empty and slug-shaped' and green on sixteen strings nobody had defined. This file defines them, and tooling/grip/ledger/disposition_owner_registry.py REFUSES anything not listed.
authority: tooling/grip/ledger/disposition_owner_registry.py is the only reader; adding a roles[] entry is pds-owner-onboarding-owner's call.

derived_from_the_ledger.note: The slug list below is DERIVED FROM THIS WALK, not quoted from the task row that asked for it. The task recorded 16 slugs on 2026-07-30 and 22 on 2026-07-31; today's walk finds 22 distinct owners board-wide and 16 live on rows whose disposition is open. An enumeration is a snapshot: re-run --derive before trusting these counts, and use --check for the verdict.

expiring_owner_ruling.why: The two honest options were auto-reassign-on-close and refuse-outright. Auto-reassign needs a writer, and disposition_owner has no code writer repo-wide — there is nothing to hang the reassignment on, so 'auto-reassign' would have been a documented intention, not an enforced rule. Refusal is enforceable by the same predicate that enforces the registry, and it fails LOUDLY at assignment time instead of silently at wave close.
expiring_owner_ruling.enforced_by: is_expiring_owner() in tooling/grip/ledger/disposition_owner_registry.py. It is checked BEFORE registry membership, so a wave-N slug is refused even if someone adds it to roles[] — and lint_registry() reds on a registry that lists one.

roles.definition: Owns the PDS shell/exs harnesses under scripts/pds-* and their door-census dispositions.
roles.resolution: Route to whoever is running the current PDS wave's harness slice; the work is a scripts/pds-* edit plus a door-census row.

roles.definition: The lead of the PDS epic for the wave that is currently open.
roles.resolution: Resolve to the named lead of the open PDS wave at the time the row is read; if no PDS wave is open the row is unassigned work and waits for the next wave.

roles.definition: Owns .claude/workflows/bp-pds-charter.md — rulings, D-numbers, and charter currency.
roles.resolution: Only a charter ruling discharges it; a worker proposes the ruling in a PR body and the epic lead applies it to the charter.

roles.definition: Owns the ONIX/Bokbasen export path and the cost/peak measurements taken against it.
roles.resolution: Route to the export lane; the work lands under api/lib/barkpark/plugins/onix* and scripts/pds-export-*.

roles.definition: Owns the task/document schema fields the PDS ledger reads and writes.
roles.resolution: Route to the api/ lane; any change is a schema v2 field change plus a migration.
Route to the import lane; the work lands under api/lib/barkpark/plugins and its ingest tests.

roles.definition: Owns repo-level hygiene: stray files, gitignore, doc tiers, budget overflow.
roles.resolution: Route to any lane; the work is repo-wide and needs no epic context.

roles.definition: Owns this registry: admitting a new role slug, retiring one, and ruling on a refused owner.
roles.resolution: The only role that may add a `roles[]` entry here; a PR touching roles[] names this owner in its body.

roles.definition: Owns the bp task ledger itself — row shape, claim/close mechanics, census walks.
roles.resolution: Route to the api/ or cli lane depending on whether the fix is server-side or in bp.

roles.resolution: Route to the deploy lane; the work lands in that script and its _test.sh.

roles.definition: Owns the api/ half of the epic's honesty class: a check that greens on a name instead of a fact.

roles.resolution: Route to the papers lane; the work lands in scripts/pds-pre-gate-papers-*.

refused.reason: Carries spaces and parentheses; breaks the ratified lowercase-kebab shape on 26 rows. A prose phrase is not an addressable owner.
refused.remedy: Re-adjudicate each row to a pds-* durable role above; there is no legal substitute, because the phrase names a DIFFERENT epic's lead.

refused.reason: Well-shaped, but it is the lead of the TRUTH-GRIP epic, not of PDS. 22 of its 23 occurrences were minted by one shard (pds-w25 `bare`) whose sibling shard in the same wave used the pds-* vocabulary instead. These rows point at an entity that does not own them.
refused.remedy: Re-adjudicate to a pds-* durable role, or file the row under the truth-grip epic. Not admissible as a PDS owner.

refused.reason: wave-N is an EXPIRING owner: it self-clears when the wave closes and the row silently degrades to unowned. See the expiring_owner_ruling below.
refused.remedy: Reassign to a durable role before the wave closes.

refused.reason: Same as wave-24; wave 25 is closed, so this row is already de facto unowned.

refused.remedy: Reassign to the durable role that owns that task's domain.

refused.reason: The row names ITSELF as its owner (verified 2026-09-11: the slug resolves to a task row, and that row is the one carrying it). Self-ownership is the defect this epic opened with; it survives among the terminal rows.
